description:
Yueyang Hangao is a name from tea history more than a tea you can reliably buy. It is listed among the Tang-dynasty teas of Hunan, alongside Jietan and Qujiang Bopian, and it belongs to Yueyang.

How it was made is not known in any useful detail. Gao means paste, which invites guesses about the leaf, but guesses are all they are.

If a shop offers this name today, ask what it actually is, since a long pedigree is easy to borrow. For a taste of Yueyang now, try Junshan Yinzhen.
history: Tang-period Hunan is credited with this tea among its early named products. Little is documented about how long the name stayed in use or whether anything links it directly to modern Yueyang teas.
